Jake (voice): 'On this Grabette, what does the actual connection interface to the two grippers look like? I'd like to take some ideas from this and some ideas from our current Generalist hand, so maybe we could make that Gen 8.' results.identified_issue: Source: packages/grabette/urdf/grabette_right/ at b5bacab06c19 (onshape-to-robot output). export_models.py does URDF forward kinematics (rpy = Rz*Ry*Rx). WORLD maps URDF (x,y,z)->(-x,-z,-y) mm, so the proximal joint axis becomes world Y about the origin, and the poses.js hinge {match ^Finger, pivot 0, sign +1, exported 90} reproduces FK; check_geometry.py verifies this. Gallery angle = proximal_deg + 90 (URDF limits [-90,0], 0 = open). Distal joint fixed at 0. Explode offsets are heuristic: 0.9*(part bbox centre - group centre), plus 0.6*(group centre - body centre) for finger groups. STLs are gitignored, so a fresh checkout needs fetch_grabette.py, which caches the clone in ~/HelpingHands-tools/cache/grabette. Uncommitted local edits (untracked files owned by others): Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map (+v008 -> 8), Two Finger Gripper/README.md, references/generalist/GENERATIONS.txt. Scripts/check_gripper_closure.py skips Gen 8 because it pairs hinges two at a time and Gen 8 has one; its existing FAILs for Gens 1-7 were already there. Chose the full grabette_right URDF (37 meshes) over the *_viewer variant (30 meshes) because it is the complete assembly.
results.summary: Gen 8 is now Pollen's real Grabette, built from their own files. It opens in the gallery, and Explode and the open/close slider both work.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 8 is exactly the Grabette, with no merging and no redesign. I took Pollen's right-hand Grabette files (github.com/pollen-robotics/grabette, pinned to commit b5bacab, Apache-2.0). Then I put each of their 73 parts where their own URDF puts it: shell, grip, Raspberry Pi and box, OAK-D camera, battery, fisheye camera, every screw, the finger and the soft tips. No shape was changed. The only change is turning the whole model so it sits upright in the viewer.

It's live in the gallery as Gen 8. Tap Explode and the parts fly apart by sub-assembly (body, finger, tip). The slider closes the one moving finger against the fixed thumb, just as Pollen's joint does, from 79 mm open to tips touching. A check confirms the slider puts every finger part within 0.01 mm of where Pollen's URDF says it goes.

Licence: Pollen's LICENSE, NOTICE and third-party notices are copied in unchanged next to the files. One thing to know: their 37 meshes (34 MB) aren't committed, because this repo ignores .stl files. Running fetch_grabette.py brings them back byte-for-byte from Pollen's repo. It checks every file against a recorded fingerprint, so it fails loudly if upstream ever changes. The tip's passive flex joint is held straight. To show Gen 8 in the gallery, I also added one line to Scripts/publish_designs.py and pointed the Two Finger Gripper README at Gen 8. Both files are untracked local files I didn't create, so those edits aren't committed.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake. Gen 8 is now the real Grabette: Pollen's own parts, put together exactly as their design places them, with nothing merged or redesigned. Open Gen 8 in the gallery and tap Explode to pull it apart, or use the slider to open and close the finger. Their licence and notice files sit right next to the files.
